summary: Elevated 5xx for single tenant during high-rate short streaming sessions causing runtime termination
description: Customer LexiDocs reported a sharp rise in 5xx responses observed beginning 2026-03-13 10:20 UTC. Errors are concentrated on streaming endpoints for a single tenant on Dedicated capacity. Symptoms: API gateway returns 502/503 to clients; backend serving-runtime processes for the tenant are observed to be OOM-killed or terminated by a GPU driver watchdog during short, high-frequency streaming sessions. Impact: Several production customers using LexiDocs' document ingestion pipeline experienced failed uploads and degraded ingestion throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a client in us-east, open 50 parallel short-lived streaming sessions (each session sends ~1-3 small frames and closes) to the streaming completion endpoint with tenant token for LexiDocs. 2) Repeat ramp for 3 minutes. 3) Observe increased 5xx responses and occasional runtime exits in the tenant pool.
logs: Attached snippets from apigw access logs: repeated HTTP/2 PING and small frames, connection churn. Serving-runtime stderr shows 'GPU_DRIVER: watchdog-kill: process terminated during memory compaction' and 'kv-cache warmup lock contention: queue length 1200'. Kernel logs show driver reset events around 2026-03-13T10:24:12Z.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: short-lived streaming sessions cause extreme KV cache churn and synchronous prefetch attempts. Prefetch workers repeatedly attempt to load KV shards for nearly-empty prefixes causing GPU memory fragmentation and triggering driver-level watchdog resets. Observed correlation between tenant's session churn and increase in 'memory compaction' logs from the NV driver. No system-wide metric anomalies outside the dedicated pool.
temporary_workaround: 1) Ask LexiDocs to reduce streaming concurrency to <10 parallel short sessions per tenant token while we investigate. 2) Apply a tenant-level throttle rule (temporary rate cap) and enable 'collapse-short-sessions' in apigw routing to coalesce close-open sessions for this tenant. 3) Pin requests to a lower-memory model variant for the tenant via routing policy.
resolution: Investigation ongoing. Engineering has deployed a config change in the dedicated pool to lower kv-cache prefetch concurrency for the affected tenant and enabled conservative GPU driver memory allocation flags in the runtime as a patch. Early metrics show 60% reduction in runtime restarts and 5xx volume. Next steps: implement a targeted kv-cache backoff algorithm and ship a runtime patch to defer large compaction ops during high connection churn. Follow-up scheduled with LexiDocs for 2026-03-16.
